policy.novelty_rule: Novelty is assessed from method and observable overlap, never from absence of an identical title.

sources.title: The Texas Spoofing Test Battery: Toward a Standard for Evaluating GPS Signal Authentication Techniques
sources.input: controlled GPS L1 C/A authentic and spoofed RF recordings
sources.audit_relevance: Defines the primary dataset and why scenario reuse is developmental rather than blind.

sources.title: GNSS Spoofing and Detection
sources.input: surveyed RF, correlation, spatial, navigation, and cryptographic observables
sources.audit_relevance: Establishes that observability depends on attacker capability; coherent synthesis is a required boundary case.

sources.title: Detailed Analysis of the TEXBAT Datasets Using a High Fidelity Software GPS Receiver
sources.input: TEXBAT RF through a configurable software receiver
sources.method: receiver-observable characterization including timing, power, and code/carrier range-rate divergence
sources.audit_relevance: Directly warns that TEXBAT contains scenario-specific artifacts and already reports global code/carrier divergence.

sources.title: Spoofing Detection by Distortion of the Correlation Function
sources.input: full delay-Doppler correlation function, simulations, TEXBAT, and live data
sources.method: propagation-channel decomposition and maximum-likelihood ratio test
sources.audit_relevance: Makes peak/CAF decomposition a prior-art and already-tested family, not a new candidate.

sources.title: GNSS Signal Authentication via Power and Distortion Monitoring
sources.venue: IEEE Transactions on Aerospace and Electronic Systems
sources.method: joint power-distortion hypothesis test with multipath class
sources.audit_relevance: Shows that fusing power with morphology is established and cannot rescue a renamed morphology model.

sources.title: Intermediate Spoofing Strategies and Countermeasures
sources.input: code phase and carrier phase measurements
sources.method: code/carrier phase consistency test derived from intermediate-spoofing strategies
sources.audit_relevance: Direct prior art for candidate 1 and the main reason its novelty score is 1/5.

sources.title: A GNSS Spoofing Detection Method Based on the Consistency of Measured and Calculated Carrier Dopplers
sources.input: tracking-loop Doppler, satellite geometry, and receiver motion

sources.title: GNSS Spoofing Discrimination Based on Doppler Residual Monitoring
sources.authors: Zhou, Li, Chen, Zhong, and Lu
sources.method: Doppler-positioning residual SSE and random traversal
sources.audit_relevance: Covers cross-PRN Doppler residual and emitter discrimination near candidate 1 and GCMR/GCSPO.

sources.title: GNSS Spoofing Detection via Self-Consistent Verification of Receiver's Clock State
sources.input: pseudorange, Doppler, and receiver clock state
sources.audit_relevance: The closest recent method to candidate 1's core closure; eliminates a strong novelty claim.

sources.title: Characterization of the Ability of Low-Cost GNSS Receiver to Detect Spoofing Using Clock Bias
sources.audit_relevance: Further narrows candidate 1's solution-level novelty and highlights receiver dependence.

sources.title: Research on the Responses of GNSS Tracking Loop to Intermediate Spoofing
sources.input: simulated tracking loops under intermediate spoofing
sources.audit_relevance: Shows that counterfactual tracking response is established prior art and receiver-parameter dependent.

sources.title: GNSS Spoofing Detection in Handheld Receivers Based on Signal Spatial Correlation
sources.input: amplitude and Doppler correlations from a moving antenna
sources.audit_relevance: The common-emitter mechanism needs spatial excitation; a stationary single front end lacks this identifying information.

sources.title: GNSS Spoofing Detection and Mitigation Based on Maximum Likelihood Estimation
sources.method: maximum-likelihood signal-parameter estimation and hypothesis testing
sources.audit_relevance: Makes mixture decomposition an established comparator for MOSAIC/MIRAGE-style proposals.

sources.title: GNSS Spoofing Detection Using Machine Learning and Truncated Singular Value Decomposition
sources.input: RF representations from TEXBAT and OAKBAT
sources.method: ConvNet with truncated SVD plus autoencoder anomaly variant
sources.audit_relevance: Demonstrates that a generic deep encoder over RF features is neither an untested observable nor sufficient novelty.

sources.title: GCI-GANomaly: A Novel GPS Spoofing Detection Scheme Based on Grayscale Constellation Image
sources.venue: IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security
sources.input: post-despreading I/Q constellation images, TEXBAT, and a collected RF dataset
sources.method: RF fingerprint image with GANomaly latent score
sources.audit_relevance: Very close to repository RF-fingerprint work; does not establish cross-receiver or source-independent identification for this audit.

sources.title: An Accurate GNSS Spoofing Detection Method Based on Multiscale Eye Diagrams
sources.input: correlator-derived eye diagrams, simulations, and TEXBAT cases 1-3
sources.method: multiscale Canny edge extraction and eye-height threshold
sources.audit_relevance: A contemporary example of correlation morphology; excluded by the no-repackaging rule.

sources.title: Global Navigation Satellite System Spoofing Attack Detection Using Receiver Independent Exchange Format Data and Long Short-Term Memory Algorithm
sources.audit_relevance: Shows that normal-looking sequence models over receiver observables are not a physical novelty by themselves.

sources.title: SSRL-UAVs: A Self-Supervised Deep Representation Learning Approach for GPS Spoofing Attack Detection in Small Unmanned Aerial Vehicles
sources.method: self-supervised representation learning followed by spoofing detection
sources.audit_relevance: Confirms that self-supervision is an existing learning strategy, not an independent physical observable or a cure for receiver/session shortcuts.
